title: Base change for $Rf_!$ on the localizing category
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: fix a prime $\ell$ and a
field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$; all schemes are separated and of finite
type over $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms. Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible coefficient
in the sense of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type and
let $v:Y'\to Y$ be a morphism in this setting (so $Y'$ is a standing scheme), with $Y'$ qcqs.
Form the cartesian square with $f':X'=X\times_YY'\to Y'$ and $u:X'\to X$. For a
compactification $f=p\circ j$, $j:X\to\overline X$, let $f'=p'\circ j'$ be its base
change, with $v':\overline X'=\overline X\times_YY'\to\overline X$. Then:

1. there is a canonical isomorphism $v'^*j_!\simeq j'_!u^*$ of functors
$D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to D(\overline X'_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$;
2. the composite
$\beta:v^*Rp_*j_!\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rp'_*v'^*j_!\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rp'_*j'_!u^*$
of proper base change and (1) is an isomorphism of functors
$\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))\to\Loc(\Dctf(Y',\Lambda))$;
3. $\beta$ is compatible with the comparison isomorphisms between
compactifications of $f$ and of $f'$.

proof.text: The pulled-back factorization is a compactification by [lemma-nagata-compactification-base-change]. On module sheaves, the right adjoints of $v'^*j_!$ and $j'_!u^*$ are respectively $j^*v'_*$ and $u_*j'^*$, by [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek-adjunction], [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], and [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. For a pro-etale $V\to X$, open restriction is localization of the site [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization](1). Both right-adjoint values on $V$ are the value of the given sheaf on $V\times_X X'=V\times_{\overline X}\overline X'$ by [def-sfb-finite-lower-star]. Their actions are the same coefficient restriction by [def-sfb-module-lower-star]. These identifications commute with restriction maps, hence give a natural module-functor isomorphism $u_*j'^*\simeq j^*v'_*$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to the common-right-adjoint identification in step 1, giving the canonical isomorphism $O_c:v'^*j_!\simeq j'_!u^*$. All left adjoints here are exact: extension by zero by [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek], and pullback by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Apply $O_c$ termwise to complexes and localize, using the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], to prove (1). Its open restriction is the identity: identify $j^*j_!$ and $j'^*j'_!$ with the identity by the canonical open units [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. The right-adjoint identification in step 1 is the identity on objects over $X'$, so the unit equation defining $O_c$ becomes $j'^*O_c=\mathrm{id}_{u^*}$. The ringed-site open-unit statement applies to these internal module objects through [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], preserving section groups and module actions. Thus this normalization is canonical, not a choice of an abstract isomorphism.

source.place: Clause (1), conjugation, termwise descent and its unit normalization

proof.text: All schemes in the compactifications and their pullbacks are in the standing setting, so both $p$ and $p'$ are proper between standing schemes. By [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback], $v^*,u^*,v'^*$ preserve $\Dctf$, direct sums and the localizing closures. By [det-proper-image-localizing-open], $j_!K\in\Loc(\Dctf(\overline X,\Lambda))$ when $K\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$. Apply [det-sf-comp-coherence-single] to $c=(j,p)$ and to its base change $c'=(j',p')$. Together with the pullback statement this puts $v^*Rp_*j_!$ and $Rp'_*j'_!u^*$ in $\Loc(\Dctf(Y',\Lambda))$; Step 2 identifies the latter with $Rp'_*v'^*j_!$. This uses the stated conclusions of those nodes, not the proof of an extension node. On $\Dctf(\overline X,\Lambda)$, the canonical proper base-change map is invertible by [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-finite](2) for finite $\Lambda$, [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-integral](3) for $\mathcal O_E$, and [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational](3) for $E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Here $\Dctf\subset\Dbc$ by definition, so the integral and rational clauses apply; $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathbf Q_\ell$ are the cases $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. The standing assumption on $Y'$ also permits the proper-image input for $p'$ in the integral theorem. By [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-extension] the same map is invertible on $\Loc(\Dctf(\overline X,\Lambda))$. Evaluate it on $j_!K$ and compose with $Rp'_*O_c$ to obtain the isomorphism $\beta_c$ of (2).

source.place: Clause (2): stated localizing targets and coefficient-level base change extended to the localizing closure

proof.text:
For each scheme map $a$, use $a^*\dashv Ra_*$ on the ordinary unbounded module-object categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], with exact pullback [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Write $B_a:b^*Ra_*\to Ra'_*b_1^*$ for the unit/square/counit mate of $a'^*b^*\simeq b_1^*a^*$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. This is the same map as in step 3. Pullback composition is the conjugate of module pushforward composition by [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp]. Each $\Mod_{\Lambda_T}$ is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], transported along the equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. The derived normalization lemma [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization], applied to these exact adjoints between Grothendieck abelian categories, therefore identifies the conjugate derived comparison with the canonical comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. The latter applies to internal modules through [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. In these coordinates, [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2),(3) gives the equality
$$B_{ab}=(Ra'_*B_b)\circ(B_aRb_*).$$
The pullback square for $ab$ is the pasted one: on sections the two iterated fiber products are canonically identified, and the scalar-extension associator sends $((m\otimes x)\otimes y)\otimes z$ to $m\otimes xyz$ in either order. Thus the pasting uses the specified maps and composite units and counits.

source.place: Clause (3), normalized derived composition and mate pasting

proof.text: Let $c_a=(j_a:X\hookrightarrow Z_a,p_a:Z_a\to Y)$, $a=1,2$, be arbitrary compactifications of $f$, and put $F_c=Rp_*j_!$. Choose a common scheme-theoretically dense refinement $d=(j_d:X\hookrightarrow D,q:D\to Y)$ with maps $h_a:D\to Z_a$ by [det-nagata-refinement-common-dense]. Let primes denote base change along $v$. Do not assume that $d'$ or $c_a'$ is dense. Apply the finite-family clause of the same node to $c_1',c_2',d'$ to obtain a scheme-theoretically dense compactification $d''=(j'':X'\hookrightarrow W,r:W\to Y')$, with refinements $k:W\to D'$ and $k_a:W\to Z_a'$. Both $h'_ak$ and $k_a$ are $Y'$-morphisms from $W$ to $Z_a'$ extending the given map on $X'$. Since the source $d''$ is scheme-theoretically dense, [det-nagata-refinement-morphisms](3) gives $h'_ak=k_a$. Every cited compactification open is quasi-compact. The bases $Y,Y'$ are qcqs by the statement and standing setting, as required by the common-dense-refinement node. For a refinement $h$ with dense source, even if its target is not dense, apply [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange](2),(3) with $p=\mathrm{id}$, $i$ the target open, and $r=h$. This supplies $e_h:j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_*j_{\mathrm{source}!}K$ on the localizing domain, uniquely normalized to identity on the open. Define $\rho_h=Rp_*e_h$ followed by the inverse proper-composition comparison of step 4. The compactification comparisons of [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle] are therefore computed as $\phi_{c_2,c_1}=\rho_{h_2}^{-1}\rho_{h_1}$, and after base change as $\phi_{c_2',c_1'}=\rho_{k_2}^{-1}\rho_{k_1}$. All refinements for which an $e$ or $\rho$ is used here have dense source $d$ or $d''$, not the possibly nondense $d'$.

source.place: Clause (3): dense replacement of all pulled-back compactifications and identification of refinement maps

proof.text:
Use the notation of step 5 and let $v_a:Z_a'\to Z_a$, $w:D'\to D$ be the projections. Denote by $O_a,O_d$ the open comparisons of step 2. For $K$ in the localizing category, consider, in the proper-composition coordinates of step 4, the maps with source $v_a^*j_{a!}K$ and target $Rk_{a*}j''_!u^*K$:
$$L_a=e_{k_a,u^*K}\circ O_a,$$
$$M_a=Rh'_{a*}(e_{k,u^*K})\circ Rh'_{a*}(O_d)\circ B_{h_a,j_{d!}K}\circ v_a^*(e_{h_a,K}).$$
Here $h_a'k=k_a$ by step 5. Pullback preservation [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback] puts $u^*K$ in the required localizing category. A refinement has inverse image of the target open equal to its source open and is identity there. Hence [lem-sfb-base-change-identity-open-restriction] applies to $h_a$ and $v_a$: the restriction of this precise $B_{h_a}$ is identity. Each $e$ restricts to identity by [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange](2), and each $O$ does so by step 2. Both $L_a$ and $M_a$ therefore restrict to identity on $X'$. Apply the uniqueness clause of interchange (2) with $p=\mathrm{id}_{X'}$, $i=j_a'$, and dense compactification $X'\hookrightarrow W\xrightarrow{k_a}Z_a'$; after $O_a$ it implies $L_a=M_a$. Only $W$ is required dense, not $D'$.

source.place: Clause (3), restriction of the mate and dense-source uniqueness

proof.text:
Apply $Rp'_{a*}$ to $L_a=M_a$ from step 6 and precompose with $B_{p_a,j_{a!}K}$. Naturality in $e_{h_a}$ moves $v_a^*e_{h_a}$ past $B_{p_a}$. The proper factors then become $(Rp'_{a*}B_{h_a})\circ(B_{p_a}Rh_{a*})=B_q$ by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2),(3), with the normalized comparisons of step 4. The remaining open factors are $O_d$ followed by $e_k$, precisely the factors in $\rho_k\beta_d$. On the other side they are $O_a$ followed by $e_{k_a}$. Thus, naturally in $K$,
$$\rho_{k_a}\beta_{c_a}=\rho_k\beta_dv^*(\rho_{h_a}):v^*F_{c_a}\longrightarrow F_{d''}u^*.$$
Every $\rho$ used here has dense source $d$ or $d''$ as specified in step 5.

old_proof.text:
*(1)* Both $v'^*j_!$ and $j'_!u^*$ are left adjoint to the same functor
$u_*j'^*\simeq j^*v'_*$ (restriction to an open commutes with direct image, as
in [det-sf-comp-coherence-single]); hence they are canonically isomorphic.
Concretely, both restrict to $u^*$ on the open $X'\subset\overline X'$ and vanish
on its closed complement, which characterizes extensions by zero (Stacks, Tag
09AH). Both functors are exact on sheaves, so the isomorphism passes to
derived categories termwise.

*(2)* The functor $v^*$ is exact, preserves direct sums and carries
$\Dctf(-,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(-,\Lambda)$ (flat constructible models for finite
rings, pulled-back local coefficient models otherwise), so it preserves
$\Loc(\Dctf(-,\Lambda))$; the same holds for $u^*$ and $v'^*$. For
$K\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$ we have $j_!K\in\Loc(\Dctf(\overline X,\Lambda))$ by
[det-sf-comp-coherence-single], so proper base change for $p$ along $v$ on
the localizing category ([sk-prop-proper-base-change-unbounded]) gives
$v^*Rp_*j_!K\simeq Rp'_*v'^*j_!K$, and (1) gives $Rp'_*v'^*j_!K\simeq Rp'_*j'_!u^*K$.

*(3)* Let $h:Z'\to Z$ be a refinement of dense compactifications of $f$, with
base change $h':Z'_{Y'}\to Z_{Y'}$, a refinement of compactifications of $f'$
(not necessarily dense; [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle] allows dense
replacement). The two composites $v^*Rp_*j_!K\to Rp'_*Rh'_*j''_!u^*K$ obtained
by first comparing compactifications and then base changing, or conversely,
are both obtained by applying $Rp'_*$ to maps
$v_Z^*j_!K\to Rh'_*j''_!u^*K$ which restrict to the identity of $u^*K$ over the
open $X'$ (the refinement maps and the isomorphism (1) restrict to identities,
and proper base change for $h$ is compatible with restriction to the open
$X'$ on which $h'$ is the identity). By adjunction for the open immersion,
such a map is unique, so the two composites agree; hence $\beta$ is
independent of the compactification.
